title: Exclude two cheaper BIT sink receipts after fixed-slot paired pulses
body:
No common-β choice gives an off-diagonal rank escape for the 32 directed paired-pulse start records, which represent 20 unordered pulse-pair/target starts. The fixed-slot proof grants all historical grade-1/2 donor stock and arbitrary sink decoding. All 6,208 directed anchored second removals and 11,152 directed cheaper-grade patterns fail. The independent audit checks the owner-411 bridge, every β branch and the off-diagonal mutation.

## Task and overlap

The scope extends the single-receipt start export in #7966 `3171fd2375ec8330109b9622b91e3949898cfb70`; #7953 `13a47f662901e894fee93365c7efec89f4f21fae` keeps the exterior stock fixed. The exact predecessor rosters are verified against the published archive. The scoped task is the #7852 follow-up at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`, based on `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` and #7830 `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive gives exact source identities and complete assumptions.

## Validation

Check the 16-entry manifest and run the original `two_receipt_cut.py --verify` and the independent `audit.py` as described. The cold extraction reproduced both exact receipts; the mutation introducing a grade-one bridge leak is rejected.

## Open next questions

Test genuinely distinct pulse vectors, changed nonsink routes or terminal retargets, or the class where one of the two replacements is individually more expensive but their joint price could win.
